author: ramana-maharshi
period: Composed in 1927 in Tamil (as Upadesa Undiyar); Ramana also rendered it into Sanskrit and other languages
summary: Thirty verses by Ramana Maharshi that grade the spiritual paths, from action and worship to self-inquiry.
whyRead: It is a compact map of how action, devotion, breath control and meditation relate to self-inquiry in Ramana's teaching, written by him in verse.
story: The verses were written at the request of the poet-devotee Muruganar for a poem about the sages of the Daruka forest, who believed ritual action alone could bring the highest fruit. Shiva's instruction to them became the frame for Ramana's verses.
questions: How do the different paths relate to one another?

keyTeachings.title: Action purifies but does not liberate
keyTeachings.text: Action yields results that pass away; done without desire and as an offering to God, it purifies the mind and prepares it.

keyTeachings.title: A graded sequence
keyTeachings.text: Worship, repetition of the name and meditation are ranked, each subtler than the last, leading toward stillness of mind.

keyTeachings.title: Breath and mind
keyTeachings.text: Breath regulation is described as a support for stilling the mind, since mind and breath share a common source.

keyTeachings.title: Inquiry into the source of I
keyTeachings.text: The culmination is turning attention to the source of the I, where the mind subsides and the Self shines.

relatedTexts.note: The Gita also relates action, devotion and knowledge
